title: Coefficient action and evaluation on derived Hom from a B-complex
statement: Let C be a small site, phi:R -> B a morphism of commutative ring sheaves, and r:D(B) -> D(R) the exact derived restriction functor [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let epsilon:K -> R[0] and epsilonB:KB -> B[0] be arbitrary augmented complexes, with a quasi-isomorphism u:K -> r(KB) commuting with augmentations and the coefficient map. There exist a functor F:D(R) -> D(B), a natural isomorphism theta:rF -> RHom_R(K,-) [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], and a natural transformation beta:id_D(B) -> Fr, such that for every M in D(B), r(beta_M) followed by theta_(rM) equals the canonical augmentation-induced unit rM -> RHom_R(K,rM) [def-weil-pbc-ringed-completion-unit]. There are no flatness, ideal, quotient, or completeness hypotheses.

proof.text: For an R-complex E use its functorial K-injective replacement I(E). Give Hom_R(rKB,I(E)) the B-action (b h)(k)=h(bk). The action laws follow from commutativity and the B-module axioms on KB. The restrictions commute with this action. The Hom differential is B-linear because the differential of KB is B-linear. Maps in E are induced by the replacement functor and are B-linear.

Naturality of replacement and two-out-of-three imply that a quasi-isomorphism E -> E′ induces a quasi-isomorphism between the K-injective replacements. Hom invariance makes the resulting Hom map a quasi-isomorphism. Restriction has unchanged additive cohomology, so it is also a quasi-isomorphism over B. Localize to construct F. Forgetting the action identifies rF with RHom_R(rKB,-); Hom invariance and the quasi-isomorphism u give the natural isomorphism theta by precomposition.

For a B-complex M the homogeneous evaluation m -> (k -> q(epsilonB(k)m)), zero on k outside degree zero, is B-linear under this action. Its chain-map equation follows from epsilonB d=0 and the chain-map equation for q; the degree minus one term vanishes by epsilonB d=0. Functoriality and localization make these maps beta natural in derived morphisms. Precomposing with u changes evaluation to x -> q(phi(epsilon(x))m)=epsilon(x)q(m), exactly the cochain for the canonical completion unit, with its evaluation-at-one identification. This proves the required equation. Zero complexes satisfy the same formulas; no boundedness or completeness assumption occurs.

theorem ringed_cech_hom_coefficient_action
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    {R B : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}} (φ : R ⟶ B)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{u} (siteModuleRings R))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{u} (siteModuleRings B))]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits (SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).map φ))]
    [PreservesFiniteColimits (SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).map φ))]
    (K : ringedSiteComplex R) (ε : K ⟶ ringedSiteRingComplex R)
    (KB : ringedSiteComplex B) (εB : KB ⟶ ringedSiteRingComplex B)
    (u : K ⟶ ((SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).map φ)).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj KB)
    (hu : QuasiIso u)
    (hε : u ≫ ((SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).map φ)).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map εB = ε ≫ siteRingComplexScalarUnit φ) :
    let r : ringedSiteDerived B ⥤ ringedSiteDerived R :=
      (SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{u}
        ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).map φ)).mapDerivedCategory
    ∃ (F : ringedSiteDerived R ⥤ ringedSiteDerived B)
      (θ : F ⋙ r ≅ ringedCechCompletionFunctor R K)
      (β : 𝟭 (ringedSiteDerived B) ⟶ r ⋙ F),
      ∀ M : ringedSiteDerived B,
        r.map (β.app M) ≫ θ.hom.app (r.obj M) =
          ringedCechCompletionUnit R K ε (r.obj M)
